messages:
maria: FYI hitting a weird parity bug between the Python SDK and REST on the sampleapp onboarding flow. SDK ignore's our `max_tokens` and seems to default to `token_budget` implicitly.
jon: ugh. can you paste a tiny repro? which endpoint call?
maria: using SDK client.chat.generate(model='redwood-1', prompt='hi', max_tokens=32) in sampleapp/server.py — but responses are way longer. here's the snippet:

```py
# sampleapp/server.py excerpt
resp = client.chat.generate(
    model='redwood-1',
    prompt=prompt,
    max_tokens=32,
    retry=3,
)
print(len(resp.text.split()))
```

sam: does REST do the same request shape? maybe param name mapping broken (camelCase vs snake_case)?
maria: calling REST with {"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":32} returns expected length. SDK call is different.
ricardo: check headers too. I remember a PR where we renamed `max_tokens` -> `token_budget` internally to support cost-based quotas, and SDK might be mapping but with a bug when `retry` param present.
maria: ah interesting — if I remove `retry=3` SDK returns correct length. with retry it's long. so retry interaction matters.
jon: that smells like the SDK retry wrapper replays request but mutates the param name on second attempt. maybe it serializes using an older key.
sam: can you run a tcpdump or log raw outgoing payload from SDK when retry is on vs off? simple print of `request.body` in transport layer helps.
maria: did that: first attempt body has {"max_tokens":32}; second retry attempt has {"token_budget":-1} (??). looks like defaulting bug + negative sentinel used when not set.
ricardo: negative sentinel -> fallback to unlimited length on model side. yikes.
maria: result = server got 512 tokens. that's why sampleapp exploded and cost spiked during onboarding sessions.
jon: we should patch SDK to preserve original keys across retries and add a unit test for `retry` + serialization parity with REST.
sam: also add an integration test in sampleapp CI that asserts token count < 40 for that prompt.
ricardo: filing issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2042 — summary: "Python SDK retry path mutates `max_tokens` to `token_budget` sentinel causing unlimited token requests". tagging eng-ml for model-side guard.
devex-bot: Auto-test run: sampleapp-onboard smoke test failed 1/10 with high token usage — linked to thread 1767777777
maria: thanks — opened PR to stop mutating payload in retry wrapper, added test. dropping note to docs team to document `token_budget` vs `max_tokens` mapping.
jon: also we should backfill server-side validation to reject negative token budgets rather than silently accept.
sam: +1. can we add an alert when cost per request spikes > 5x for onboarding project? that's a temporary mitigation.
ricardo: created infra alert: onboarding-cost-spike. will monitor.
maria: workaround for now: set `retry=None` in sampleapp until patch lands, and add a safe `max_allowed_tokens` guard in app.
jon: thanks for the triage — please include test vectors so we don't regress.
maria: will do, PR in review. :thumbsup:
